title: Contaminated event window: confounding news during event period

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Method: Event study with cross-sectional adjustment to partial out the confounding earnings news. Specifically, compute abnormal returns (AR) from a market model, then at event day 0 regress AR on the earnings surprise. The intercept captures the average acquisition-induced return after removing the earnings component; the slope captures the earnings-news sensitivity. We also compute an acquisition-only CAR over [-1,+1] by subtracting the earnings-driven component from day 0 and adding day −1 and +1 ARs.

Key assumptions:
- Additivity/separability: Day-0 return = acquisition effect + earnings effect + noise.
- Correct specification: Market model and pre-event alpha/beta capture normal returns; no omitted common factors that load on both eps_surprise and acquisition returns.
- Exogeneity: eps_surprise is orthogonal to the acquisition-specific shock (E[eps_surprise × acquisition_shock] = 0).
- No other confounders on day 0; limited information leakage (captured via CAR over a narrow window).
- Stable betas and alphas estimated from pre-event window (−10 to −2).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

suppressWarnings({
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(data.table)
    library(dplyr)
    library(lmtest)
    library(sandwich)
  })
})

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s18_data.csv"
dt <- fread(path)

# 2) Basic checks
req_cols <- c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta","eps_surprise")
missing_cols <- setdiff(req_cols, names(dt))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop(sprintf("Missing required columns: %s", paste(missing_cols, collapse=", ")))
}

# 3) Estimate firm-specific alpha from a pre-event window and compute AR
# Use event_day <= -2 as the clean pre-window
pre_alpha <- dt %>%
  filter(event_day <= -2) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(alpha_hat = mean(ret - beta * mkt_ret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups="drop")

dt <- dt %>%
  left_join(pre_alpha, by="stock_id") %>%
  mutate(AR = ret - (alpha_hat + beta * mkt_ret))

# Drop firms with missing alpha (insufficient pre-window data)
valid_firms <- dt %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(any_alpha = all(!is.na(alpha_hat)), .groups="drop") %>%
  filter(any_alpha) %>% pull(stock_id)

dt <- dt %>% filter(stock_id %in% valid_firms)

# 4) Main decomposition at event day 0: AR0 ~ eps_surprise
d0 <- dt %>% filter(event_day == 0) %>%
  select(stock_id, AR0 = AR, eps_surprise) %>%
  filter(!is.na(AR0), !is.na(eps_surprise))

if (nrow(d0) == 0) stop("No valid day-0 observations after preprocessing.")

fit_main <- lm(AR0 ~ eps_surprise, data = d0)
vc_main  <- vcovHC(fit_main, type = "HC1")
ct_main  <- coeftest(fit_main, vcov = vc_main)

acq_day0_est <- unname(coef(fit_main)[1])          # intercept = acquisition effect (avg)
acq_day0_se  <- sqrt(diag(vc_main))[1]
acq_day0_t   <- acq_day0_est / acq_day0_se

earn_beta_est <- unname(coef(fit_main)[2])         # slope on eps_surprise
earn_beta_se  <- sqrt(diag(vc_main))[2]
earn_beta_t   <- earn_beta_est / earn_beta_se

# 5) Acquisition-only CAR over [-1, +1]: subtract earnings component only on day 0
dm1 <- dt %>% filter(event_day == -1) %>% select(stock_id, AR_m1 = AR)
dp1 <- dt %>% filter(event_day == 1)  %>% select(stock_id, AR_p1 = AR)
car_base <- d0 %>%
  left_join(dm1, by="stock_id") %>%
  left_join(dp1, by="stock_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(AR_m1), !is.na(AR_p1))

# CAR_i^acq = AR_{-1} + [AR_{0} - beta_eps*eps_i] + AR_{+1}
car_base <- car_base %>%
  mutate(CAR_acq_i = AR_m1 + (AR0 - earn_beta_est * eps_surprise) + AR_p1)

CAR_acq_mean <- mean(car_base$CAR_acq_i, na.rm = TRUE)
CAR_acq_sd   <- sd(car_base$CAR_acq_i, na.rm = TRUE)
CAR_acq_n    <- sum(!is.na(car_base$CAR_acq_i))
CAR_acq_se   <- CAR_acq_sd / sqrt(CAR_acq_n)
CAR_acq_t    <- ifelse(CAR_acq_se > 0, CAR_acq_mean / CAR_acq_se, NA_real_)

# 6) Print main results
cat("Main results (abnormal returns in decimal units):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Day-0 acquisition effect (intercept): % .4f  [SE: %.4f, t: %.2f, N: %d]\n",
            acq_day0_est, acq_day0_se, acq_day0_t, nrow(d0)))
cat(sprintf("  Earnings sensitivity (slope on eps_surprise): % .4f  [SE: %.4f, t: %.2f]\n",
            earn_beta_est, earn_beta_se, earn_beta_t))
cat(sprintf("  Acquisition-only CAR [-1,+1]: % .4f  [SE: %.4f, t: %.2f, N: %d]\n\n",
            CAR_acq_mean, CAR_acq_se, CAR_acq_t, CAR_acq_n))

# =========================
# Robustness checks
# =========================
cat("Robustness checks:\n")

# (A) Alternative alpha window: use [-10, -3]
pre_alpha_alt <- dt %>%
  filter(event_day <= -3) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(alpha_hat_alt = mean(ret - beta * mkt_ret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups="drop")

dt_alt <- dt %>% select(-AR) %>%
  left_join(pre_alpha_alt, by="stock_id") %>%
  mutate(AR_alt = ret - (alpha_hat_alt + beta * mkt_ret))

d0_alt <- dt_alt %>% filter(event_day == 0) %>%
  select(stock_id, AR0 = AR_alt, eps_surprise) %>%
  filter(!is.na(AR0), !is.na(eps_surprise))

fit_alt <- lm(AR0 ~ eps_surprise, data = d0_alt)
vc_alt  <- vcovHC(fit_alt, type = "HC1")
acq_day0_est_alt <- unname(coef(fit_alt)[1])
acq_day0_se_alt  <- sqrt(diag(vc_alt))[1]
acq_day0_t_alt   <- acq_day0_est_alt / acq_day0_se_alt
cat(sprintf("  (A) Day-0 acquisition effect with alpha window [-10,-3]: % .4f  [SE: %.4f, t: %.2f]\n",
            acq_day0_est_alt, acq_day0_se_alt, acq_day0_t_alt))

# (B) Nonlinearity in earnings response: add quadratic term
fit_quad <- lm(AR0 ~ eps_surprise + I(eps_surprise^2), data = d0)
vc_quad  <- vcovHC(fit_quad, type = "HC1")
acq_day0_est_quad <- unname(coef(fit_quad)[1])
acq_day0_se_quad  <- sqrt(diag(vc_quad))[1]
acq_day0_t_quad   <- acq_day0_est_quad / acq_day0_se_quad
cat(sprintf("  (B) Day-0 acquisition effect with quadratic earnings term: % .4f  [SE: %.4f, t: %.2f]\n",
            acq_day0_est_quad, acq_day0_se_quad, acq_day0_t_quad))

# (C) Winsorize extreme AR0 at 1% tails
q_lo <- quantile(d0$AR0, probs = 0.01, na.rm = TRUE)
q_hi <- quantile(d0$AR0, probs = 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)
d0_w <- d0 %>% mutate(AR0_w = pmin(pmax(AR0, q_lo), q_hi))
fit_win <- lm(AR0_w ~ eps_surprise, data = d0_w)
vc_win  <- vcovHC(fit_win, type = "HC1")
acq_day0_est_win <- unname(coef(fit_win)[1])
acq_day0_se_win  <- sqrt(diag(vc_win))[1]
acq_day0_t_win   <- acq_day0_est_win / acq_day0_se_win
cat(sprintf("  (C) Day-0 acquisition effect (winsorized AR0 at 1%% tails): % .4f  [SE: %.4f, t: %.2f]\n",
            acq_day0_est_win, acq_day0_se_win, acq_day0_t_win))

# (D) Panel day-effects with earnings control at day 0 (centered eps)
# Merge eps_surprise at day 0 to all event days to ensure availability
eps_by_firm <- d0 %>% select(stock_id, eps_surprise)
dt_panel <- dt %>%
  left_join(eps_by_firm, by = "stock_id", suffix = c("", ".d0")) %>%
  mutate(eps_c = eps_surprise - mean(eps_surprise, na.rm = TRUE))

# Refit on rows with non-missing AR and eps_c
dt_panel2 <- dt_panel %>% filter(!is.na(AR), !is.na(eps_c))
fit_panel <- lm(AR ~ 0 + factor(event_day) + I(event_day == 0):eps_c, data = dt_panel2)
vc_panel  <- vcovHC(fit_panel, type = "HC1")
coefs_panel <- coef(fit_panel)
ses_panel   <- sqrt(diag(vc_panel))
# Coefficient on factor(event_day)0 is the mean day-0 AR at average eps_surprise (acquisition-only)
nm <- names(coefs_panel)
idx0 <- which(nm == "factor(event_day)0")
if (length(idx0) == 1) {
  acq_day0_panel <- unname(coefs_panel[idx0])
  acq_day0_panel_se <- ses_panel[idx0]
  acq_day0_panel_t  <- acq_day0_panel / acq_day0_panel_se
  cat(sprintf("  (D) Day-0 acquisition effect from panel day dummies + eps control: % .4f  [SE: %.4f, t: %.2f]\n",
              acq_day0_panel, acq_day0_panel_se, acq_day0_panel_t))
} else {
  cat("  (D) Panel check: day-0 coefficient not found (check factor coding).\n")
}

cat("\nDone.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Day-0 acquisition effect (intercept): modestly negative, around −0.5% to −1.0%. Rationale: acquirers often see negative abnormal reactions due to winner’s curse, integration risk, and potential overpayment.
- Earnings sensitivity (slope on eps_surprise): positive; a 1-unit standardized earnings surprise typically maps to about +2% to +4% return on day 0.
- Acquisition-only CAR over [−1, +1]: more negative than day-0 alone, around −1% to −2%, as markets may incorporate acquisition news over the immediate window while earnings effects are largely captured by the slope at day 0.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with confound adjustment — regress AR on eps_surprise + acquisition dummy
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: After controlling for earnings surprise, acquisition announcement generates negative AR
